section_1.title: The Hook: What is Topology?
section_1.content: Introduce topology as 'rubber-sheet geometry.' Explain that in topology, distance and angles don't matter—only connectivity and continuity remain. If you can deform an object into another without tearing or gluing, they are topologically equivalent (homeomorphic).
section_1.example: An animation showing a coffee mug being smoothly stretched and morphed into a donut (torus) while keeping the handle hole intact.

section_2.title: The Golden Rule: Invariants
section_2.content: Define 'Invariants'—properties that stay the same despite continuous deformation. Focus on the 'Genus' (the number of holes). Explain that a sphere has 0 holes, a torus has 1, and a pretzel has 3. These numbers distinguish shapes regardless of how they are stretched.
section_2.example: Visualizing a balloon character (0 holes) vs. a physical whistle (1 hole); showing that no matter how much you squeeze the balloon, it can never become the whistle.

section_3.title: The Classic Proof: Euler's Characteristic
section_3.content: Introduce the formula V - E + F = 2. Vertices (V), Edges (E), and Faces (F). Explain that for any convex polyhedron, this value is constant. This is the bridge between rigid geometry and flexible topology.
section_3.example: A 3D cube counting exercise: 8 vertices - 12 edges + 6 faces = 2. Then, showing how this holds true even if the cube is 'dented' or distorted.

section_4.title: Real-World Application: The Seven Bridges of Königsberg
section_4.content: Briefly mention how Leonhard Euler solved the problem of crossing seven bridges exactly once by treating the landmasses as 'nodes' and bridges as 'lines.' This birthed Graph Theory, a branch of topology.
section_4.example: A map of Königsberg where the city layout transforms into a simple point-and-line diagram, proving the journey is impossible.

section_5.title: Conclusion: Why it Matters
section_5.content: Summarize that topology is the foundation of modern data analysis, robotics path planning, and even understanding the shape of the universe.
section_5.example: A quick visual montage of a robot arm calculating its path (topology) and a map of a neural network connection.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
